predictions.selection_reason: user-controlled input -> encode operation through external library -> potential encoding vulnerability
predictions.source_summary: Input comes from function parameter 'input' which is user-provided string data. The operation supports multiple character encodings from IO_FORMAT including UTF-8, UTF-7, Windows codepages, ISO standards, and various language-specific encodings.
predictions.sink_summary: Encoded output is stored in a JSON object and returned. The 'present' method later displays this as HTML table content using Utils.printable() for sanitization.
predictions.guard_summary: Operation runs in try-catch block handling encoding errors. Utils.printable() in presentation provides some output sanitization. No explicit input validation or encoding-specific security controls observed on the encoding path.
predictions.risk_pattern: User-controlled string input is encoded through multiple character encodings using external library (cptable) without validation, potentially enabling encoding-based injection or interpretation issues if malformed input exploits encoding-specific behaviors.
predictions.context_summary: Part of TextEncodingBruteForce operation that enumerates all supported text encodings for input. In encode mode, converts string to various character encodings using cptable library and converts result back to string representation.
unresolved_facts: Specific security implications of cptable.utils.encode() implementation
Potential encoding-specific vulnerabilities in the cptable library
Whether Utils.printable() provides sufficient output sanitization for all encoding scenarios
